The Svensk Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Svensk Icon of the Theotokos

Svena · Svensk-Pechersk · Mother of God of the Kyiv Caves

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Svensk composition shows the enthroned Mother of God with Christ between Anthony and Theodosius of the Caves. The OCA associates its veneration with Bryansk.

[1] Opening iconographic identification

What is depicted

The displayed Kyiv-school panel is catalogued around 1288 and belongs to the Tretyakov Gallery. The two Caves founders stand at either side of the throne, holding texts. Its old paint and damaged edges are visible. The object’s catalogue date is distinguished from the traditional attribution to Alypios, who lived earlier.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The received account attributes the icon to Alypios and tells of its 1288 journey from Kyiv to heal Prince Roman of Chernigov. The icon is found in an oak beside the Svena River; the prince regains sight and establishes a monastery. The account later describes rescue and restoration after the monastery’s closure.

[1] Prince Roman,foundation and preservation

Published explanation

Antonova and Komova’s 2021 study explicitly examines the foundation legend as a literary and artistic source. Its abstract relates the enthroned Virgin to the Kyiv-Caves altar mosaic and identifies the founders’ figures as early surviving portraits. This scholarly treatment of the story and the actual icon is distinct from treating every element of the legend as independently documented contemporary fact.

[3] English research abstract
